REASONING:

Step 1 - Frame the Project
- Objective: Improve the quality of tourism infrastructure and services, the conditions of natural and cultural heritage sites, and increase sustainable tourism activity in the Arequipa-Colca corridor.
- Scope: 33 individual investment sub-projects across tourism, cultural heritage, rural transport, water/sanitation, health, and forestry/environment, alongside transversal institutional strengthening and project management.
- Delivery Model: Investment Project Financing (IPF) with IBRD loan to MEF, coordinated nationally by MINCETUR and implemented subnationally by the Regional Government of Arequipa (GORE Arequipa) through a dedicated Project Implementation Unit (PIU).
- Timeline: Expected approval Date: July 9, 2026; Closing Date: June 30, 2032 (6-year implementation horizon).
- Budget: Total operation cost of US$97.80 million (IBRD Loan: US$77.20 million; Counterpart funds from MINCETUR/GORE: US$20.60 million).
- Key Stakeholders: MEF, MINCETUR, GORE Arequipa, participating municipalities, Ministry of Culture, MTC, Ministry of Housing, SERNANP, local communities, and regional private tourism operators.
- External Dependencies: Execution of Interinstitutional Agreements with participating municipalities, multi-sector coordination across line ministries, and timely counterpart funding allocations.

Step 2 - Category Sweep
- technical:
  * High road fatality rate in Arequipa (11.7 per 100k vs 8.8 national average) requiring specialized safety designs (para 36).
  * Structural vulnerability and earthquake damage to 17th-19th century historic churches requiring specialized restoration (para 34).
- financial:
  * Budget allocation and execution delays in Peru subnational public investments affecting project readiness (para 62).
  * Potential errors in financial records/reporting due to unfamiliarity with WB financial management procedures (para 62).
- schedule:
  * Disbursement condition requiring signed Interinstitutional Agreements with at least 3 municipalities before component 1 & 2 funds unlock (Datasheet vii).
  * Risk of delayed recruitment of key PIU and FM personnel (para 62).
- stakeholder:
  * Highly fragmented institutional landscape hindering multi-sector coordination (para 6).
  * Risks of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse / Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) during civil works in rural corridors (para 20).
- political_regulatory:
  * Macro political instability in Peru threatening institutional continuity and coordination momentum (para 1, 47).
- environmental:
  * Climate hazards (heavy rains, flooding, landslides, mudslides) threatening transport corridors and heritage sites (para 11, 12, 60).
  * Degradation and forest fire risks in the high-Andean Bosque de Queñua ecosystem (para 38, 59).
- organizational:
  * GORE Arequipa lacking prior experience in implementing World Bank-financed IPF operations (para 44).
  * Potential ambiguity and unclear internal coordination roles within the newly established PIU (para 62).
- external:
  * Macro economic or external travel shocks impacting international tourist arrival growth (para 3, 53).

Step 3 - Evidence Filter
All candidate risks selected above directly quote or paraphrase specific findings in the Project Appraisal Document text.

Step 4 - Assess
Each risk evaluated for Likelihood (1-5) and Impact (1-5), supported by evidence-grounded justifications and actionable mitigations.

Step 5 - Consolidate
Consolidated into 14 core risks spanning all 8 required categories, formatted strictly per the schema.

risks.description: Initial project execution and disbursements may be delayed due to national and subnational budget allocation and execution bottlenecks.
risks.mitigation: GORE Arequipa will initiate budget allocation procedures immediately upon loan signing as prescribed in the Project Operational Manual.
risks.evidence: In Peru, initial project implementation phases often experience delays in budget allocation and low budget execution rates

risks.description: GORE Arequipa lacks experience implementing World Bank-financed operations, risking non-compliance with World Bank fiduciary, environmental, and social policies.
risks.mitigation: Deploy Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) funds for advance PIU capacity building on Bank fiduciary, environmental, and social requirements prior to effectiveness.
risks.evidence: GORE... does not have experience implementing WB-financed projects, so capacity building and close supervision will be required

risks.description: Severe weather events, heavy rainfall, flooding, and landslides linked to El Niño could damage access roads and interrupt construction and tourist mobility.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate-resilient engineering standards into road and infrastructure designs, including slope stabilization, reinforced drainage, and retaining walls.
risks.evidence: floods and resulting mudslides weaken transportation infrastructure, road closures impede access to tourism destinations

risks.description: Earthquake damage and disrepair in 17th-19th century churches could lead to structural failure or improper restoration during rehabilitation works.
risks.mitigation: Utilize traditional climate-resilient materials and structural reinforcement techniques supervised by specialized cultural heritage conservation guides.
risks.evidence: The churches were built in the 17th to 19th centuries and are in various states of disrepair, many having suffered earthquake damage.

risks.description: Delays in executing mandatory Interinstitutional Agreements with local municipalities will block loan disbursements for civil works under Components 1 and 2.
risks.mitigation: Proactively engage participating municipal authorities using GFPP resources to negotiate and execute required Interinstitutional Agreements prior to effectiveness.
risks.evidence: No withdrawals shall be made... for Parts/components 1 and 2... until and unless the Bank has received at least three signed Interinstitutional Agreements

risks.description: Delays in recruiting qualified key staff for the PIU may delay project startup and impede operational efficiency.
risks.mitigation: Finalize terms of reference for all key PIU positions early and launch competitive recruitment to ensure appointments within 60 days of effectiveness.
risks.evidence: Delayed recruitment of FM staff... Terms of reference... shall be appointed within two months after effectiveness.

risks.description: Institutional fragmentation across sector ministries and local governments could cause conflicting priorities and implementation delays.
risks.mitigation: Operationalize high-level Steering and Consultative Committees to formalize inter-institutional alignment between MINCETUR, MEF, MTC, Culture, and GORE.
risks.evidence: Efficient budgeting and implementation of investments in tourism are hindered by lack of coordination within a highly fragmented institutional landscape

risks.description: Broader political instability and administrative changes in Peru could disrupt project decision-making and momentum.
risks.mitigation: Establish an autonomous PIU structure reporting directly to the Governor and formalize binding multi-year interinstitutional commitments.
risks.evidence: The slowdown has revealed important structural challenges... in addition to increased political instability in recent years.

risks.description: Civil works and labor influx in rural tourism corridors create exposure to risks of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH).
risks.mitigation: Adopt and enforce a comprehensive SEA/SH Action Plan, worker codes of conduct, and accessible community grievance reporting channels.
risks.evidence: exposure to sexual harassment and exploitation risks

risks.description: High historical road fatality rates in Arequipa present safety risks for residents and visiting tourists along improved transport corridors.
risks.mitigation: Mandate comprehensive road safety features in road designs—such as speed calming, guardrails, markings, and pedestrian crossings—and perform safety audits.
risks.evidence: Arequipa recorded 11.7 road traffic deaths per 100,000 people, a significantly higher rate than Peru's national average

risks.description: Inadequate PIU experience with World Bank financial management procedures could result in accounting errors and delayed financial reporting.
risks.mitigation: Utilize the national SIAF system with SIAF-WB reconciliation controls, deliver early FM training, and retain independent external auditors.
risks.evidence: Inadequate experience with Bank-financed projects may result in errors in financial records and reporting.

risks.description: Global economic downturns, health crises, or regional travel disruptions could lower international tourism arrivals below project targets.
risks.mitigation: Diversify destination promotion strategy to heavily target resilient domestic and South American regional markets alongside long-haul segments.
risks.evidence: The pandemic has severely impacted the sector, and in 2025 Peru received 4.2 million international tourists, 78 percent of pre-pandemic levels.

risks.description: Ambiguity in internal roles and operational procedures within the newly formed PIU could cause coordination failures and workflow delays.
risks.mitigation: Define precise operational roles, internal control mechanisms, and decision workflows within the Project Operational Manual (POM).
risks.evidence: Unclear internal coordination and roles within the PIU.

risks.description: Uncontrolled grazing, agricultural encroachment, and wild forest fires threaten degradation of the delicate high-Andean Bosque de Queñua ecosystem.
risks.mitigation: Execute community-based forest monitoring, 174 ha of native reforestation, sustainable grazing technical assistance, and forest fire prevention training.
risks.evidence: training and technical assistance related to grazing and agriculture management, prevention of illegal activities, prevention and control of forest fires
